title: "Home Manager and the Module System"

# Home Manager and the Module System

Configuring tools per user without root permissions is the core role of Home Manager. The boring default is: **manage user-space utilities via `home.packages` and service configurations via typed `programs.<name>` options**.

## Mental model

Home Manager applies the exact same NixOS module system to non-root user environments:
1. `home.packages`: Installs packages into your user environment (`~/.nix-profile`).
2. `programs.<name>.enable = true;`: Configures shell, editors, and CLI tools, automatically placing dotfiles into `~/.config/`.
3. Standalone vs NixOS module: Can run as a standalone CLI (`home-manager switch`) on any Linux/macOS distro, or as a built-in submodule inside `configuration.nix`.

## Worked examples

Save as `home.nix`:

```nix
# home.nix
{ pkgs, ... }:

{
  home.username = "deskadmin";
  home.homeDirectory = "/home/deskadmin";
  home.stateVersion = "24.11";

  home.packages = with pkgs; [
    bat
    fzf
    jq
  ];

  programs.bash.enable = true;
}
```

Run:

```bash
home-manager switch
```

Output:

```
Starting Home Manager activation
Creating symlinks in /home/deskadmin...
Home Manager switch complete!
```

## The boring rule

- Use Home Manager for dotfiles and user tools.
- Reserve system `configuration.nix` for kernel, hardware, daemons, and system users.
